ops.statement: When a gate's deliverable is a load-bearing STATISTICAL CORRECTION (a de-biasing / residualization / normalization whose whole point is to remove a confound), an output-only synthetic recovery test ('inject the signal, confirm it recovers') CANNOT distinguish a correct correction from a broken one that recovers the confound instead. The synthetic falsifier MUST include a NEGATIVE CONTROL: (a) a generator that carries BOTH the confound AND the genuine signal as separate terms, (b) a null arm injecting ONLY the confound (zero genuine signal) that the correct correction must report ~0, and (c) an explicit broken-variant helper (e.g. the weaker correction) asserted to FAIL that null arm. Without the negative control the test is structurally blind to the exact failure the correction exists to prevent.
ops.grounding: 668-instrument-panel g3-replication: the golf-correction's first spec (per-driver demean) was output-plausible but wrong -- it left the shared class main effect, which replicates trivially (a healthy-looking replication with zero driver-utilization content). The cold plan critic caught it pre-code; the fix (double-centering) was validated by a 3-arm generator carrying a real driver x class interaction term PLUS a negative-control test asserting per-driver-demean-only FAILS the pure-shared-class arm (measured r_double=0.0006 vs r_demean=0.685). The g3 reviewer re-derived the discriminating condition from scratch (within-class the two corrections are identical to 1.1e-16, so the interaction r must span classes). An 'inject class-shape, confirm recovery' test alone would have passed BOTH the correct and the broken correction.
ops.bank_reason: One occurrence so far (this golf-correction instrument). Re-observe on the next load-bearing de-biasing/residualization gate whether an output-only recovery test again masks a broken correction and whether the negative-control-plus-interaction-generator recipe generalizes, before graduating it into commander-core.md's crew-gate / falsifier-design guidance.
